Name: TMeasy tire - bicycle (bias ply)
Notes: Lateral characteristics fitted to Dressel & Rahman, 'Measuring sideslip and camber characteristics of bicycle tyres', Vehicle System Dynamics (2011), doi:10.1080/00423114.2011.615408 (references/bicycle_tire_sideslip_2015.pdf). The paper measured 23-28 mm road tyres at 220-440 N, so its load-normalized values are applied here at the vehicle's ~2.2 kN wheel load (an extrapolation). The paper gives no longitudinal, vertical, or rolling data; those entries are assumptions described in Derivation.

Derivation.Lateral: Fig. 11 (Fy/Fz vs slip angle, 0-3.6 deg) gives 11/rad for the bias-ply tyres (Bon) and 9/rad for the radial tyre (Maxxis), matching the values in Sec. 4.4. The bias-ply set was fitted, because utility/rickshaw tyres are bias ply. TMeasy fit with peak mu 0.90: initial stiffness 12.0, peak slip 0.15 (RMS error 0.05 in Fy/Fz; 11.9/rad secant at 1 deg; 0.64 at 3.6 deg vs 0.64-0.72 measured). The peak mu (0.90) and the 0.78 at 5 deg match the saturation in Kyle's data reproduced in Fig. 1. Peak slip is the smallest the curve allows (2 * peak mu / initial stiffness).
Derivation.Load_sensitivity: Kyle's data in Fig. 1 (200-490 N) shows Fy/Fz at 2 deg dropping about 12% per doubling of load, while the saturation level hardly changes. The double-load lateral stiffness scale is 1.75 and the peak mu scale 0.95.
Derivation.Longitudinal: Not measured in the paper. Assumed: the baseline tire's longitudinal/lateral stiffness ratio (18/14) applied to the fitted lateral value, with peak mu 0.05 above the lateral value as in the baseline. Peak slip 0.13 is the smallest the curve allows. Load-sensitivity scales are kept from the baseline.
Derivation.Vertical: Not measured in the paper. Stiffness and damping are kept from ThreeWheeler_Tire.json, so a comparison with the baseline isolates the force characteristics. Bottoming deflection is 0.030 m, the rim-pinch travel of a ~37-40 mm section tire (ETRTO 37-622 / 40-635).
Derivation.Rolling_resistance: Not measured in the paper. 0.006 is a typical bicycle tire value on a road surface.

Paper_reference_data.Note: Informational only; the quasi-steady TMeasy element has no camber input or transient lag.
